label: Getting work done
rationale: The work itself: using your head, delivering results, taking notes, ideas coming to you, stamping papers.
mixUps: kekka o dasu (you deliver results) is not kekka ga deru (results come out); ideas come to you with ga ukabu, while notes are taken with o toru.

targets.english: use your head; make you think
targets.use: Said as a blunt scolding (chotto wa atama tsukae yo, use your head for once) and about brain-heavy games and work: atama tsukau shigoto. Casual speech often drops o.
targets.notes: Not ki o tsukau, which means being considerate.

example.romaji: kono geemu, kekkou atama tsukau ne.
example.ja: このゲーム、結構頭使うね。
example.english: This game really makes you think.

examplePolite.romaji: kono geemu wa kekkou atama o tsukaimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: このゲームは結構頭を使いますね。
examplePolite.english: This game really makes you think.

targets.verbSense: put out, take out, send out; here: produce
targets.trap: 'Get results' tempts kekka o morau. Results you achieve are put out: kekka o dasu. Results being announced is kekka ga deru, and kekka o morau only fits being handed a results sheet.
partners: kiroku (record: kiroku o dasu = set a record)
targets.use: Said about performance at work, in sport or in study, often as a must: kekka dasanai to (I need to show results). Casual speech drops o.
targets.notes: Learn it beside kekka ga deru: kekka deta (they're out) vs kekka dashita (I delivered).

example.english: This year I'm going to get results, no matter what.

examplePolite.romaji: kotoshi wa zettai kekka o dashimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今年は絶対結果を出します。
examplePolite.english: This year I'm going to get results, no matter what.

targets.use: Said in class, meetings and on the phone: chotto matte, memo toru kara. Casual speech drops o, and memo suru means the same and is at least as common.
targets.notes: A note left for someone is memo o nokosu.

example.ja: ちょっと待って、メモ取るから。
example.english: Hang on, let me write that down.

examplePolite.romaji: chotto matte kudasai, ima memo o torimasu node.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと待ってください、今メモを取りますので。
examplePolite.english: Just a moment, let me write that down.

targets.politeJa: アイデアが浮かびます
targets.trap: 'I've got an idea!' is ii kangae ga aru! (or ii aidea aru!, omoitsuita!). ukabu is for ideas coming, or not coming, to mind: nanimo ukabanai.
targets.use: Mostly in the negative, while brainstorming or choosing a gift: nanimo ukabanai (nothing comes to mind). When one arrives, ii aidea ukanda! Casual speech drops ga.
targets.notes: omoitsuku is the active twin: ii koto omoitsuita!

example.ja: 全然いいアイデア浮かばない。
example.english: I can't come up with any good ideas.

examplePolite.ja: 全然いいアイデアが浮かびません。
examplePolite.english: I can't come up with any good ideas.

targets.trap: 'Stamp' leads to sutanpu, which means a rubber stamp for fun or a chat sticker. A personal seal is a hanko (formally inkan), and you press it: hanko o osu.
targets.use: Heard at the bank, the city office, at work and for deliveries: koko ni hanko oshite kudasai. Casual speech drops o; for deliveries a signature usually works too: sain de ii desu ka?
targets.notes: Banks and contracts want the registered inkan; deliveries usually accept a sain (signature).

example.ja: ここにハンコ押してね。

examplePolite.romaji: koko ni hanko o oshite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: ここにハンコを押してください。

reviewPool.english: snow settles, lies on the ground
put time into, take time over
set aside time, take up time
